findings.evidence: Proof body lines 159-165 already routes through `FDRep.of ρ` / `ind_ofFDRep` / `character_mem_virtualCharacters (V : FDRep k G)` (VirtualCharacter.lean:107). Roadmap README.md:70: "results about `Ind χ` are stated for `FDRep`"; VirtualCharacter.lean:56-61: "`FDRep.of` mediates between the two, and nothing is lost".
findings.fix: State `theorem ind_ofFDRep_mem_virtualCharacters (S : Subgroup G) [S.FiniteIndex] (A : FDRep k S) : ((ind S (ofFDRep A) : ClassFunction k G) : G → k) ∈ virtualCharacters k G`, proved by `rw [ind_ofFDRep, ...]; exact character_mem_virtualCharacters _`, and apply it at line 238 with `FDRep.of ρ` plus `(ofFDRep_eq_ofCharacter _).symm`.
findings.issue: `ind_ofCharacter_mem_virtualCharacters` is stated only for `ρ : Representation k S (Fin n → k)`, but the proof immediately converts to `FDRep.of ρ` and applies `character_mem_virtualCharacters`, which is an `FDRep` statement. The general fact — an induced character of any finite-dimensional representation of a subgroup is a virtual character — is strictly stronger and one line shorter; the `Fin n → k` case follows by `ofFDRep_eq_ofCharacter`.

findings.evidence: Roadmap README.md:44: "carry `[S.FiniteIndex]` as an explicit hypothesis; over a finite `G` it is automatic but we never bury it." The neighbouring `ind_ofFDRep` (Character.lean:227) follows this; the new lemma does not.
findings.fix: Move the lemma out of the `[Finite G]` variable block and carry `[S.FiniteIndex]` explicitly, matching `ClassFunction.ind_ofFDRep [S.FiniteIndex]` in Character.lean:227.
findings.issue: `ind_ofCharacter_mem_virtualCharacters` inherits `[Finite G]` from the variable block, but nothing in the statement or proof needs it: `ind` needs only `[S.FiniteIndex]` (Induction/ClassFunction.lean:264), `indFDRep` needs only `[S.FiniteIndex]` (FiniteDimensional.lean:256), and `virtualCharacters` needs only `[Monoid G]`. This is a strictly stronger hypothesis than the result requires.

findings.evidence: Spanning.lean:136-138 states the problem itself: "The definition does not unfold outside this module, so this is what a downstream proof rewrites with." Artin.lean:219-222 is that rewrite plus a from-scratch re-derivation of the span the definition already records.
findings.fix: Drop both `cyclic*` definitions and their `_eq_inducedFrom`/`_eq_inducedCharactersFrom` lemmas, and state the cyclic corollaries (`cyclicInduced_eq_top`, `cyclicInducedCharacters_eq_top`, `ind_mem_cyclicInduced`, the `exists_sum_smul_*` forms) directly about `inducedFrom k G {S | IsCyclic S}` / `inducedCharactersFrom k G {S | IsCyclic S}`; Artin.lean can then apply `inducedCharactersFrom_eq_top` without unfolding and without rebuilding `𝒢`.
findings.issue: `cyclicInduced` (:133) and `cyclicInducedCharacters` (:260) are the general definitions applied to the set literal `{S | IsCyclic S}` and add no content, but give the same submodule a second name. Being opaque under the module system they force two `rfl` bridging lemmas (:139, :265) and, in Artin.lean:219, a `▸` rewrite past `cyclicInducedCharacters` followed by re-declaring the generating set `𝒢` (Artin.lean:212-217) and re-proving `span k 𝒢 = ⊤` from `inducedCharactersFrom_le_iff` — because neither the cyclic nor the general definition exposes its generating set. `cyclicInduced` has no consumer at all outside this file.

summary: The public lemma `ind_ofCharacter_mem_virtualCharacters` is stated below its natural level — restricted to representations on `Fin n → k` and assuming `[Finite G]` where only `[S.FiniteIndex]` is used — contrary to two explicit roadmap conventions. Separately, the `cyclicInduced`/`cyclicInducedCharacters` definitions are contentless specializations of the general-family definitions that add a second name for the same submodule and force `rfl` bridging lemmas.
